newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS - Portugal inflation homes in on EMU goal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Portugal inflation homes in on EMU goal.

text.p: Portugal's inflation rate, once seen as its economic Achilles heal, is falling close to levels needed for entry to the European single currency, according to official figures released on Tuesday.
The National Statistics Institute (INE) said that the year-on-year rate in March dipped to just 2.5 percent from 2.9 percent in February, exceeding the most optimistic forecasts.
Analysts had seen a rate of 2.6 to 2.7 percent.

With the late spring and summmer months likely to bring more good inflation news, analysts say that the latest figure takes Portugal well down the road to meeting its price target of an average 2.25-2.50 percent for the year as a whole.
The rolling 12-month average currently stands at 3.2 percent.

A rate of around 2.5 percent is generally regarded as sufficient for entry to economic and monetary union (EMU) which sets a ceiling of 1.5 percentage points above the average of the three best-performing member states.

"We are on the road to fulfilling the prices criterion set down in the Maastricht Treaty (the single currency blueprint)," said analyst Jorge Ferraz of research group Informacao Mercados Financeiros. "The year-on-year rate surprised me. I had only expected it in April or May," he added.
The news gave a fillip to local financial markets which saw the inflation figure as clearing the way for the Bank of Portugal to cut interest rates again.

Even the Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, which has staked its political credibility on qualifying for monetary union in the first wave in 1999, had seen inflation as Portugal's toughest economic test.
But Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said recently that inflation had been more restrained over the first three months than the government had expected when it drew up its financial plans.
Analyst Isabel Costa of Banco Finantia said that the result in March meant that Portugal's inflation could even end the year below the 2.5 percent target.
"It is a very favourable number. This improves the inflation outlook for the end of the year," she said.

Analysts say that the year-on-year rate should dip to near two percent at the start of the summer as meat price rises last year, triggered by the mad cow disease scare, drop out of the index. The rate will pick up again slightly towards the end of the year.
